title: Two-week water storage
h1: Two-week water storage: containers, cleaning and rotation
dek: Which containers are safe, how to sanitize them, where to keep them, and how to keep the stock fresh without it becoming a forgotten chore. All from the CDC and FEMA, with our reasoning kept separate.
description: How to store emergency water safely: bottled vs self-filled, food-grade containers, CDC sanitizing steps, storage conditions, labeling and six-month rotation.
recheck: If CDC or Ready.gov revises the storage guidance, or at the next quarterly source sweep.

source_use.cdc-water-store: Bottled water first; container choice and what to avoid; wash, sanitize, shake, wait, dry, fill; labeling; six-month replacement; temperature range; light and toxin separation; clean scoop; bleach to keep on hand.
source_use.ready-water: Store commercially bottled water sealed in its original container in a cool, dark place; food-grade containers; sanitizing solution; non-commercial water replaced every six months.
source_use.usscm-brenckle-2019: Captain Porter's 1812-13 account of cask cleaning and seasoning for ship's water (history panel only).
